feasibility.verdict: Feasible as an idealized single-factor sensitivity experiment. Clay fraction is a mineral soil property that ELM maps to hydraulic parameters (via pedotransfer/Clapp-Hornberger or van Genuchten), so a controlled sweep holding forcing, PFT, and all other soil properties fixed cleanly isolates its effect on surface runoff vs. deep recharge partitioning.
answerable: Direction and magnitude of change in surface runoff (QOVER) vs. deep drainage/recharge (QDRAI) as clay increases from 5% to 55%
How infiltration capacity, saturated hydraulic conductivity, and soil moisture storage shift the partitioning
Whether the response is monotonic or saturates across the clay gradient
Effect on evapotranspiration as a competing sink that mediates the partition
not_answerable: Site-specific validation against observed runoff/recharge (no observations provided)
Lateral/subsurface flow interactions (single-column has no lateral connectivity)
Effects of clay-dependent macropore/preferential flow not represented in default ELM hydrology
Interactions with sand/silt co-variation (only clay is varied here; texture triangle closure is assumed)

parsed.n_justification: Six identical columns differing only in prescribed clay fraction (5, 15, 25, 35, 45, 55%) evenly span the requested 5-55% range, enough to resolve monotonicity and any saturation/threshold behavior in the runoff/recharge partition while keeping the design minimal and interpretable.
requires_capabilities: user-modifiable surface dataset to prescribe fsand/fclay per column
ELM default VIC/TOPMODEL runoff and Richards-based subsurface hydrology
history output at monthly and daily (h1) resolution for flux budgeting
assumptions: All columns share identical lat/lon, PFT, LAI, topography, forcing, and soil-color/organic properties; only clay (and complementary sand/silt) fraction differs.
Sand and silt are adjusted to close the texture fractions to 100% while keeping sand comparably low so that clay is the dominant varied control.
First ~5 years treated as spin-up/equilibration; analysis focuses on the quasi-steady period to remove initial-condition memory.
Recharge is diagnosed from QDRAI/QRECHARGE (bottom drainage below the root zone) and runoff from QOVER; ET (QFLX_EVAP_TOT) is tracked as the competing water sink.
Default ELM pedotransfer relationships translate clay fraction to hydraulic conductivity, porosity, and matric potential parameters.
No lateral groundwater exchange beyond the single-column baseflow parameterization.
